A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLM-guided RMD framework and InterPlay dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including v1's image-based appendix material.

before.justification: v1 Section 4 and Tables 2–3 report original simulation results for six interaction skills, long-horizon tasks, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 Section 4 and Tables 2–3 retain original simulation results and ablations and add evaluated TokenHSI comparisons.

M1.justification: The stated per-pair RMD reward changes from unsquared norm penalties in v1 Appendix C to squared penalties in v2 Equation 16. Figure A2 also adds an explicit reasoning sequence to the planner prompt. These are limited revisions within the retained GPT-4V/RMD reinforcement-learning framework; implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions cover carrying, pushing, opening, sitting, lying, and reaching, plus static, dynamic, and hybrid long-horizon interactions. The same asset-source datasets and 1,210 InterPlay plans are retained. The newly disclosed 117-asset count does not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: TokenHSI is added as an evaluated comparator in both single-task and long-horizon experiments. AMP, InterPhys, and UniHSI retain their respective participation. Changes to the conceptual feature comparison in Table 1 do not establish additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated scene-construction protocol is tightened: v1 Section 4.2 permits optional contextual objects, whereas v2 Appendix B requires at least two furniture items alongside its interactive-object requirement. Single-task randomization, 20 cm thresholds, and 4096 evaluation trials are retained. Newly documented training budgets and stages do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The object-part, human-part, position, velocity, dynamics-encoding, and VLM-versus-LLM ablations are retained. The one-multi ablation becomes one-one with the same description and scores. The household case study's 15 panels are regrouped from Figures 13–20 into Figures A4–A8, rather than replaced by new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without training-seed repetitions, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: TokenHSI result rows are added. Between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2, static long-horizon completion changes from 11.4% to 21.3% for InterPhys and from 31.2% to 37.2% for UniHSI. The reason is unspecified. RMD, existing ablation scores, and other retained numerical entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal reward definitions change: for example, v1 Appendix C Equation 15 uses exp(-||p||_2), whereas v2 Equation 16 uses exp(-||p||_2^2), with analogous changes to velocity penalties. This changes the mathematical objective. The reorganized graph notation largely restates existing mathematics; neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first unified physics-based HOI framework leveraging VLMs in its abstract and contributions, strengthening the novelty assertion. The underlying contributions—RMD-based automatic goal/reward construction, diverse long-horizon interactions, and InterPlay—remain. Performance superiority was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: New Appendix E identifies single-agent scope and difficulties with extended temporal reasoning and hierarchical household tasks, including cooking and interconnected tidying. It proposes multi-agent learning and improved planning as future directions. These add concrete applicability boundaries absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 Appendices B–C newly document asset selection and processing, manual plan review, network sizes, PD action targets, two-stage training, and extensive PPO hyperparameters in Table A1. The reported proprioceptive vector changes from 276 dimensions including object information to 223 character dimensions, and the project link changes. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds Grove, TokenHSI, InterScene, Lingo, and additional scene-synthesis references, while refocusing Table 1 on physics-based control, guidance granularity, planning, and unified policies. Its criticism of Eureka shifts from interpretability and motion naturalness to iterative-search cost. The broader HOI positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial method explanations are rewritten. Separate RMD-definition and planner sections are combined, long-horizon experiments precede single-task experiments, and dataset construction moves into an expanded appendix. The appendix gains a contents list and reorganized sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to show goal-state and reward construction, Table 1 changes its comparison structure, and Figure 3 is rearranged. Appendix prompts and case-study panels are consolidated, and a new hyperparameter table is added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 supplies substantially better implementation documentation, adds the TokenHSI comparison, and states concrete limitations, making the paper easier to reproduce and assess. Most empirical evidence is retained, and revised reward/state specifications are not reconciled with the unchanged RMD scores. The overall gain is therefore limited.
